current_activity: XII Corps attack on Blerick: flails breach the minefields, AVREs bridge an anti-tank ditch, and Kangaroos carry the infantry through cleared lanes
notes: Event date: 3 December 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 159). Event definition: XII Corps, with strong artillery and Typhoon support, makes a well-planned attack on Blerick, a suburb of Venlo on the left bank of the Meuse. Flails breach the minefields, bridge-crossing AVREs bridge an anti-tank ditch, and Kangaroos take the attacking infantry close to their objective by lanes cleared through the enemy defences; from that point the taking of the town is a walk-over. Ellis does not name the infantry division that entered the town; the specialist armour (flails, AVREs and Kangaroos) is recorded on the 79th Armoured Division, which provided those teams. Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 159: "On December the 3rd, with strong artillery and Typhoon support, XII Corps made a well-planned attack against Blerick. Flails were used to breach minefields, bridge-crossing AVREs to bridge an anti-tank ditch and Kangaroos (armoured personnel carriers) to take the attacking infantry close to their objective by lanes which had been cleared through the enemy defences: from that point the taking of the town proved to be a walk-over." Location: Blerick, Venlo, Limburg (new place PL4014) with a precision of 3 km.
